literal: Even though being in a high position, those who do not have noble character are not noble; even though being in a low position, those who do not have base character are not base.
translation: Even when placed in high positions, those who lack noble qualities are never noble; and even when placed in low positions, those who lack base qualities are never base.
modern: உயர்ந்த நிலையில் இருந்தாலும், மேன்மையான குணம் இல்லாதவர்கள் மேலானவர்கள் அல்லர்; தாழ்ந்த நிலையில் இருந்தாலும், இழிவான குணம் இல்லாதவர்கள் தாழ்ந்தவர்கள் அல்லர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that true greatness or baseness is determined solely by one's character, not by social status or position. The poet uses the words 'mēl' (high/noble) and 'kīḻ' (low/base) in two distinct senses: physical or social position, and moral character. A person of low character does not become noble simply by being elevated to a high position. Conversely, a person of noble character does not become base even when forced into a lowly position.
